title: Impact of Elite High School Admission on SAT Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD), using the admission-test score as the running variable and the admission cutoff as the threshold. Students just above the cutoff are compared to those just below it using local linear regression with a triangular kernel.
- Why: Admission is determined by a score threshold; near the cutoff, treatment status is as good as random conditional on the score. This isolates the causal impact of elite school admission on subsequent SAT outcomes.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: Potential outcomes (SAT scores absent admission) are continuous in the running variable at the cutoff.
  - No precise manipulation: Students cannot precisely sort around the cutoff.
  - If compliance is imperfect (fuzzy RD), we additionally use the Wald ratio (reduced-form jump in SAT divided by the first-stage jump in treatment) to recover the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for compliers at the cutoff, assuming exclusion and monotonicity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis (RDD: sharp and fuzzy if needed)
# - Prints a clear numerical result
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# --------------- Setup ---------------
# No external packages required; base R implementation with fallbacks.

# Helper: find cutoff by maximizing the jump in admission probability
find_cutoff <- function(x, d, min_each_side = 30) {
  ux <- sort(unique(x))
  if (length(ux) < 3) return(median(x))
  mids <- (ux[-1] + ux[-length(ux)]) / 2
  best_jump <- -Inf
  best_c <- median(x)
  n <- length(x)
  for (c in mids) {
    left <- which(x < c)
    right <- which(x >= c)
    if (length(left) < min_each_side || length(right) < min_each_side) next
    pL <- mean(d[left], na.rm = TRUE)
    pR <- mean(d[right], na.rm = TRUE)
    jump <- pR - pL
    if (is.finite(jump) && jump > best_jump) {
      best_jump <- jump
      best_c <- c
    }
  }
  return(best_c)
}

# Helper: choose a simple bandwidth (rule-of-thumb) and ensure enough observations
choose_bw <- function(x, min_frac = 0.2, max_iter = 20) {
  n <- length(x)
  sd_x <- stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(sd_x) || sd_x <= 0) sd_x <- diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / 4
  h <- 1.84 * sd_x * n^(-1/5)  # rule-of-thumb start
  if (!is.finite(h) || h <= 0) h <- diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE)) * 0.2
  # Inflate h until at least min_frac of sample lies within the window
  target <- ceiling(min_frac * n)
  i <- 0
  while (sum(abs(x) < h) < target && i < max_iter) {
    h <- h * 1.25
    i <- i + 1
  }
  # Cap h to avoid swallowing whole sample
  maxh <- 0.9 * max(abs(x), na.rm = TRUE)
  h <- min(h, maxh)
  return(h)
}

# Helper: local-linear RD with triangular kernel; order=1 (linear) or 2 (quadratic)
local_linear_rd <- function(y, x, h, order = 1) {
  Tind <- as.integer(x >= 0)
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(x) / h)
  keep <- which(w > 0 & is.finite(y) & is.finite(x))
  yk <- y[keep]; xk <- x[keep]; Tk <- Tind[keep]; wk <- w[keep]
  if (length(yk) < 20) {
    return(list(est = NA, se = NA, v = NA, pval = NA, ci = c(NA, NA), h = h, n = length(yk)))
  }
  if (order == 1) {
    fit <- lm(yk ~ Tk + xk + I(Tk * xk), weights = wk)
    cname <- "Tk"
  } else {
    fit <- lm(yk ~ Tk + xk + I(xk^2) + I(Tk * xk) + I(Tk * xk^2), weights = wk)
    cname <- "Tk"
  }
  s <- summary(fit)
  est <- coef(fit)[cname]
  se <- s$coefficients[cname, "Std. Error"]
  pval <- s$coefficients[cname, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  ci <- est + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se
  v <- as.numeric(vcov(fit)[cname, cname])
  list(est = as.numeric(est), se = as.numeric(se), v = v, pval = as.numeric(pval),
       ci = as.numeric(ci), h = h, n = length(yk))
}

# --------------- Load data ---------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s90_data.csv"
dat <- tryCatch({
  read.csv(path)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Could not read CSV at: ", path, " | Error: ", e$message)
})

# Basic checks
req_cols <- c("running_var", "treated", "y")
if (!all(req_cols %in% names(dat))) {
  stop("Data must contain columns: running_var, treated, y")
}

# --------------- Determine cutoff ---------------
c_hat <- find_cutoff(dat$running_var, dat$treated, min_each_side = 30)
x <- dat$running_var - c_hat

# --------------- Main RD (local linear, triangular) ---------------
h0 <- choose_bw(x, min_frac = 0.25)
main_y <- local_linear_rd(y = dat$y, x = x, h = h0, order = 1)

# First-stage jump in treatment (to diagnose sharp vs fuzzy)
fs <- local_linear_rd(y = dat$treated, x = x, h = h0, order = 1)
pi_hat <- fs$est
pi_se  <- fs$se

# Fuzzy RD (Wald) TOT if necessary
wald_est <- NA; wald_se <- NA; wald_ci <- c(NA, NA)
if (is.finite(pi_hat) && abs(pi_hat) > 1e-6) {
  wald_est <- main_y$est / pi_hat
  # Delta method ignoring covariance (conservative)
  wald_var <- (main_y$v / (pi_hat^2)) + ((main_y$est^2) * (fs$v) / (pi_hat^4))
  wald_se <- sqrt(wald_var)
  wald_ci <- wald_est + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * wald_se
}

# --------------- Robustness checks ---------------
# Bandwidth variation
half_bw <- local_linear_rd(y = dat$y, x = x, h = max(h0 / 2, .Machine$double.eps), order = 1)
dbl_bw  <- local_linear_rd(y = dat$y, x = x, h = h0 * 2, order = 1)

# Higher-order polynomial
quad_bw <- local_linear_rd(y = dat$y, x = x, h = h0, order = 2)

# Placebo cutoff (+/- 10% IQR of running_var)
iqr_rv <- IQR(dat$running_var, na.rm = TRUE)
shift <- 0.1 * iqr_rv
c_placebo <- c(c_hat + shift, c_hat - shift)
placebo_out <- lapply(c_placebo, function(cpl) {
  xpl <- dat$running_var - cpl
  hpl <- choose_bw(xpl, min_frac = 0.25)
  local_linear_rd(y = dat$y, x = xpl, h = hpl, order = 1)
})

# Manipulation (density balance) check within h0
left_n  <- sum(x < 0 & abs(x) < h0)
right_n <- sum(x >= 0 & abs(x) < h0)
dens_pval <- NA
tot_n <- left_n + right_n
if (tot_n > 0) {
  # Test if right share equals 0.5 locally
  dens_pval <- binom.test(right_n, tot_n, p = 0.5, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value
}

# Compliance sharpness near cutoff (mismatch between recorded treated and indicator x>=0)
T_local <- as.integer(x >= 0 & abs(x) < h0)
obs_local <- dat$treated[abs(x) < h0]
if (length(obs_local) > 0) {
  mismatch_rate <- mean(T_local != obs_local)
} else {
  mismatch_rate <- NA
}

# --------------- Print results ---------------
cat("Regression Discontinuity Analysis: Elite High School Admission -> SAT\n")
cat("Estimated cutoff (c_hat):", round(c_hat, 4), "\n")
cat("Main local-linear RD (triangular kernel, order=1):\n")
cat("  Bandwidth h:", round(main_y$h, 4), " | N within h:", main_y$n, "\n")
cat("  Discontinuity in SAT at cutoff (ITT):", sprintf("%.4f", main_y$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", main_y$se), 
    ", 95%% CI: [", sprintf("%.4f", main_y$ci[1]), ", ", sprintf("%.4f", main_y$ci[2]), "], p-value:",
    sprintf("%.4f", main_y$pval), ")\n", sep="")

cat("First-stage (jump in admission at cutoff):\n")
cat("  pi_hat:", sprintf("%.4f", pi_hat), " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", pi_se), ")\n")

if (is.finite(pi_hat) && abs(pi_hat) > 0.8) {
  cat("Interpretation: Near-sharp RD (large first-stage). ITT ≈ TOT.\n")
} else if (is.finite(pi_hat) && abs(pi_hat) > 0.2) {
  cat("Fuzzy RD: Wald LATE (Admission effect) at cutoff:\n")
  cat("  TOT (Wald) =", sprintf("%.4f", wald_est),
      " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", wald_se),
      ", 95% CI: [", sprintf("%.4f", wald_ci[1]), ", ", sprintf("%.4f", wald_ci[2]), "])\n", sep="")
} else {
  cat("Warning: Very weak first-stage; TOT not reported (unstable).\n")
}

cat("\nRobustness checks:\n")
cat("- Bandwidth half (h/2): ITT =", sprintf("%.4f", half_bw$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", half_bw$se), ")\n")
cat("- Bandwidth double (2h): ITT =", sprintf("%.4f", dbl_bw$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", dbl_bw$se), ")\n")
cat("- Quadratic polynomial (same h): ITT =", sprintf("%.4f", quad_bw$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", quad_bw$se), ")\n")
cat("- Placebo cutoff (+10% IQR): ITT =", sprintf("%.4f", placebo_out[[1]]$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", placebo_out[[1]]$se), ")\n")
cat("- Placebo cutoff (-10% IQR): ITT =", sprintf("%.4f", placebo_out[[2]]$est),
    " (SE:", sprintf("%.4f", placebo_out[[2]]$se), ")\n")
cat("- Density balance near cutoff (binomial test for left=right within h): p-value =",
    ifelse(is.na(dens_pval), "NA", sprintf("%.4f", dens_pval)), "\n")
cat("- Compliance mismatch within h (recorded treated vs. score-based indicator):",
    ifelse(is.na(mismatch_rate), "NA", sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mismatch_rate)), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Modestly positive. Elite school admission at the margin likely yields small gains in SAT performance due to peer effects and resources, but prior literature often finds limited returns on standardized test outcomes at selective thresholds.
- Magnitude: Approximately 0.05–0.10 SD in SAT scores at the cutoff (ITT). If the design is fuzzy and the first-stage is <1, the TOT (admission effect) would be larger than the ITT by roughly 1/π; for example, with π ≈ 0.8, a 0.06 ITT implies a TOT ≈ 0.075.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare SAT scores of students just above and below the admission cutoff.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Admission to the elite high school slightly decreases SAT scores.
